steps.content: With the West District business wrapped up smoothly today, you're now left with half a day to spare, and you already know how to spend it.
Parfait's evasiveness about her past—and those mysterious friends of hers—has only sharpened your curiosity. If she won't talk, you'll find the answers yourself.

Based on what you've learned from days of investigation and grilling Eastside reporters for leads, it takes you several hours to locate a run-down apartment building. By the time you match the address in your notes to a faded door number, night shadows stretch long across the hallway.
It's a typical wooden apartment door you'd see anywhere in the West District—plain, weathered, and indistinguishable from any other.
The narrow hallway is choked with debris and layered in dust, yet the space before this door stands conspicuously swept clean. Someone's been here recently.
You knock. Seconds stretch into silence. When no answer comes, your hand drifts toward the handle.
Clack!

The lock gives way—whether from years of decay or forced entry, you can't say. Just a gentle twist, and the latch releases with a shudder. Something metal drops into the shadows as the door groans open.
Clank!
The metallic clatter ricochets down the concrete corridor. Flustered, you spin around, only to discover someone standing right behind you.
You quickly raise both hands to show you mean no harm, but it's already too late.
Don't move!
A sharp shout jolts you upright. Within moments, neighbors begin to cluster around, drawn by the disturbance and already buzzing with speculation.
What's going on? Did someone break in?
Doesn't look like it...
So another one of those Eastside ************s? Great, just what we needed. Has nobody ever taught you people it's rude as hell to barge into folks' homes uninvited?

The hallway lights have been dead for years, leaving the late-night darkness thick enough to hide the neighbors' faces. Not that you need to see them clearly. The rolling pins and kitchen knives in their hands tell you everything you need to know.
Just tie them up and send them to the Executive Committee...
Send 'em my ass! Hell, how many have we sent there this month already? Screw talking. Just rough 'em up and throw 'em out on their ears. That'll make 'em learn to stay gone.
What's all the racket? That home got broken into again?
An elderly man shuffles up the stairs, his flashlight beam trembling ahead of him between raspy coughs. As he speaks, the surrounding commotion gradually dies down.
Now listen here, don't you Eastside meddlers got anything better to do than creep around at this hour pulling this kinda nonsense!

How many times do we have to tell you? There's nothing here for you. But you never listen, just keep forcing your way into that home in the middle of the night. And now look at you, caught red-handed again.
The flashlight's glare blinds you for a moment. You wince, instinctively closing your eyes.
You know what they say—enough is enough. If I let you off easy this time, you'll just... Wait a minute. Do I know you from somewhere?
Hey, I've seen you on TV... Hold on, aren't you that, uh... what's the name again? Right, the MBCC Chief!
Apparently, your reputation in the West District still carries weight. When the neighbors realize who you are, they quickly untie you and usher you into the elderly man's apartment.

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: Sorry about that, Chief. Just a simple misunderstanding, that's all. We've had some shady sorts skulking about after dark lately. Got everyone on edge, you see... Cyllis, be a dear and fetch the Chief some water.
The elderly man across from you—Rayden, you've since learned—sits with a polite but slightly embarrassed air, sighing between apologies. It's clear he's the one calling the shots in this building.
It's alright. However you slice it, me breaking into a place at night is pretty suspicious behavior.

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: Have some water, Chief.
The girl who first found you walks over from the kitchen, carrying a glass.
Thank you.
You accept the water and fake a sip—old habits die hard. They might be simple-hearted West District locals, honest as the day is long, but you've been burned too often to drop your guard now.
Speaking of which, I've been wondering something. Were all the people who broke in here at night before Eastsiders?

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: Who said that?!
Old Rayden stiffens, his gaze whipping around before zeroing in on a burly young man, the same guy who threatened to "rough you up" earlier.
No, no, I was just talking nonsense...
Before the young man can finish, Cyllis silences him with a stern glare.
The people before me were probably all from Eastside, but I think there's been a misunderstanding. They were basically just reporters or investigators.
As for me, I'm here for the same reason they were, to look into someone called "Parfait Medici"...
You lay out your intentions with no attempt to soften them. Everyone in the room suddenly falls silent, the air growing so still it feels almost eerie.

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: Who is Parfait Medici? One of you Eastsiders too?
Hard to say. That's what she calls herself, but lately Eastsiders don't seem to buy it.
So you're here to arrest this... what's-her-name, Parfait Medici? What's she even done that is bad enough to drag you all the way out here?

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: ED HOUSE—
Whether it's his loose tongue or his lack of manners that set her off, Cyllis grinds out the young man's full name through clenched teeth, her voice low but seething.
She's just involved in some financial disputes back in Eastside. Since reports indicate she's a Sinner, I thought I'd check it out myself... Nothing too serious.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Oh, nothing serious? That's good then...

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: Cough...
The old man nearby finally loses patience with the young man's clumsy act and clears his throat pointedly.

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: Chief, this Parfait Medici you mentioned... I'm afraid the name doesn't ring a bell. But we respect what you're doing here, and if there's any way we can help, you can count on us...

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: How about this? Let's call it a day for now. We'll keep our eyes peeled for this... Parfait Medici. Anything comes up, you'll be the first to know.
The name doesn't ring a bell, huh...
You stroke your chin, adopting a convincingly troubled expression.
But here's the thing, I checked the residential records with the Executive Committee, and it's right there in black and white. The owner listed for that upstairs apartment is "Parfait."

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: Uh, well...
They probably never expected you to extract anything useful from the West District's notoriously messy registration system. Everyone in the room falls silent, momentarily at a loss for words.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: ...Look, just 'cause the names are similar doesn't prove anything, y'know? And honestly, "Parfait" sounds way better than whatever... "Parfait Medici." Pfft, who even came up with that?

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: Anyway, that apartment's been empty for years. Nobody even knows who's supposed to be the owner.
It's been empty for years?
But when the door opened earlier, I got a quick look inside. Everything looked clean and tidy, not abandoned at all.
Your words hang in the air as the neighbors exchange uneasy glances. The silence stretches, their faces tightening with visible concern.
Then you catch it. Cyllis's eyes keep flicking toward the kitchen. Toward the rolling pin. Whatever they're hiding about Parfait, they're prepared to defend that secret firmly.
The atmosphere turns increasingly hostile as their stares harden. You know you need to talk your way out of this fast, before they graduate from menacing silence to something far more violent.
Hey, easy everyone. Don't worry, I'm not here to arrest Parfait. If anything, it's the opposite. We're actually friends...

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Oh, you're friends? Geez, you should've led with that...
Not so easily convinced, Cyllis cuts Ed off with a firm hand. Without you noticing, she's already palmed the rolling pin, tucking it casually behind her back.

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: So if you're this Parfait's friend, what exactly are you doing here?

She got into some trouble half a year ago. Now the Eastsiders are claiming she's actually some con artist from the West District, connected to that big counterfeiting case a few years back. That's why she asked me to wipe any evidence that could be used against her.

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: Oh? She asked you, an Eastside "enforcer," to "wipe evidence" for her? This Parfait must be seriously connected.
Clearly, Cyllis isn't buying your story. She brings the rolling pin forward, holding it at the ready now. Her gaze locks onto yours—steady, unblinking—and the air grows thick with tension.
A long beat passes. Then, from beside the table, comes a weary sigh.

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: Alright... Just drop it, all of you. If the Chief came alone, everything must already be figured out. No sense hiding the truth now...

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: Everyone just settle down. Really now, you want to keep the Chief around for good? Then we're not just talking about fraud anymore. Parfait'd be facing much heavier charges.
As the elder's voice fills the room, the tension finally drains away. Cyllis's grip on the rolling pin loosens, her arms slowly lowering to her sides.

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: Just one thing still has me wondering, Chief. Would you mind telling me how Parfait got found out?

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: That counterfeiting business was years back now. And if I recall right, that girl made sure to pay back every cent the moment she could, didn't she?
She did that?
As if desperate to prove a point, Ed quickly jumps in.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Exactly! She's way too nice for her own good, never scammed the same mark twice, and if she ever took a bit too much, she'd beat herself up over it. Soon as she had cash, she'd quietly pay people back. Next to those Eastside sharks, she might as well be a saint!

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: If you ask me, it's definitely those fancy hobbies of hers that screwed her—always rubbing elbows with those Eastsiders. Tsk, she never stopped to think... since when do poor Syndicate folks like us get to mess around with fancy art?

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: She even called me just a few days ago, asking us to go to some Eastside concert with her...
Cyllis presses her palm on her forehead, looking exasperated.

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: Back when she was riding high, making bank for Eastsiders, nobody asked too many questions. But after what went down six months ago? Suddenly they're digging up every skeleton in her closet.
Perhaps with their defenses lowered, the complaints come pouring out, with everyone venting their frustrations at once.

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: Ever since that phone call, this place has been crawling with more snoops in two weeks than we usually see in half a year.

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: ...Not that I've got anything against concerts. I watch it myself on TV every New Year when there's nothing better to do. But this timing... ah, really couldn't be worse.

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: If we go with her, those fancy types will just look down their noses at us! Look what's happening to Parfait over in Eastside, getting hounded day and night. She'd do better coming back to the West District. At least here, she still has us watch her back.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Yeah, she'd be better off coming back! Getting pushed around and investigated in Eastside, might as well just come back here... Oh right, Chief!
The young man's head jerks up as if he's just remembered something vital. When he turns to you, his expression is disarmingly earnest.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: You're friends with Parfait, right? Why don't you talk to her? Tell her to quit running with those fancy Eastside types and just come back home.
Ed doesn't even finish his sentence before the entire room zeroes in on you. Hope flashes across their faces, but it's edged with unease.
Still, this does give you a convenient way out of the situation. Of course, you also suspect that if you refused, given how close they are to Parfait, they probably wouldn't just let you walk away.
...All right. I'll try.
The day after returning to the Bureau, you find yourself wrestling with how to bring this matter up with Parfait.
The locals from the West District aren't really as simple as they appear. That tense meeting last night made it clear: refusing them wasn't an option. Not if you wanted to walk away.
You have given your word, and you don't plan to break it. But coming clean to Parfait would mean admitting you've been investigating her behind the scenes.

After spending these days together, you've come to realize that Parfait isn't some scheming villain. If anything, she's surprisingly genuine—witty, cooperative, even good company. She already promised you she'd cooperate with the investigation after the Spring Concert. The more you think about it, the more this secrecy sits uneasily with you.
With this in mind, you head to Parfait's temporary room, only to find it empty. A full sweep of the Bureau later, you finally spot her in the mail room.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Good morning, Chief.
Parfait greets you politely before opening the envelope in her hands, revealing a thick stack of tickets inside.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Phew... Thank goodness he wasn't fooling me.
After confirming the tickets are legitimate, she exhales in relief.
Wow, how did you even get these?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I reached out to someone from the event organizers and spent forever going back and forth with him. He asked me to give a speech on stage and tried to get me to trade for the VIP ticket. Honestly, even over the phone, I could tell that guy was shady.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: But luckily, I managed to swap for twelve regular tickets... and I saved one for you! What do you think? Would you like to come with me?
Under Parfait's pure, hopeful gaze, you feel a twinge of guilt and dodge giving her a straight answer.
I'm happy for you, Parfait. Now you can take Rayden and the others to the Spring Concert.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Yeah, finally! After taking quite a bit of effort...
One moment she is animatedly recounting all the trouble she has gone through, but then—mid-sentence—she falls silent, her hand slowly lowering the tickets she's been waving in the air.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: So... you went to see them, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: No need to apologize.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: ...In the end, no deception is ever truly perfect. Sooner or later, the truth always comes out. And honestly? My identity was full of holes from the very beginning.
As she speaks, Parfait slides the tickets back into the envelope and meets your gaze.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Let's find somewhere else to talk, Chief.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: By the way... you didn't let slip anything unnecessary, did you?
Once back in the room, you quietly close the door behind you. Before you can even ask a question, Parfait speaks up first.
What do you mean by anything unnecessary?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: For instance, your opinion on the concert and things like that.
No.
Parfait lets out a sigh of relief, then offers a bitter smile as she explains.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Oh, thank goodness you didn't. They're already so hesitant about the concert. If they caught even a whiff of disinterest in you, they'd have the perfect excuse to back out.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: "Look, even the MBCC Chief doesn't want to go, so why should we bother?" Something like that... By the way, how are they doing now?
They seemed normal enough, except for apparently helping with your cover. They were being pretty cautious about it.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I see...
At the mention of this topic, Parfait sets the folder down on the table and slumps into her chair, completely deflated.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: So you've found out... Yes, I'm from the West District, and the whole Medici family heir identity is fake. Honestly, I made it up on the spot! But people actually bought it, so I just went with it and forged a complete set of identity documents...

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I did counterfeit money. It was around N.F. 108... Once in February I made ten thousand DisCoins to buy some decent clothes, and once in April I made a hundred thousand to pay a hotel bill.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Later, with my new identity and those clothes, I became a stockbroker and started earning money... And don't worry, once I could, I made sure to pay back both the tailor and the hotel for their losses.
Wait, you're telling me that huge Eastside counterfeiting case from a few years back only involved a hundred and ten thousand DisCoins total?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I swear on my life, not a penny more! Honestly, the fake cash I whipped up with my Sinner ability was too good. When they stumbled on bills with duplicate serial numbers and couldn't tell them apart from the real ones, the whole market freaked...

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I was terrified when it happened. Me? Accidentally crashing economies? Not exactly the legacy I was going for, so I never dared touch counterfeiting again after that.
Seeing the once-glorious investment guru now reduced to this pitiful state in front of you, you can't help but feel amused as you ask.
Is that all there is to your criminal record?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I... think so? If you're going to accuse me of cheating investors after I became a stockbroker... but I made them huge profits every single time... Honestly, I have no idea why things worked out that way. I don't really understand professional finance, so I just went with my gut.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: And somehow... it worked every single time. I practically just tripped into becoming the "investment guru." But as my reputation grew over the past few years, I barely dared make any moves. Too terrified my luck would finally run out and get myself exposed...

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Honestly, I'm not shocked at all that you uncovered my whole story. The real miracle is that it took this long! I suppose it's because I finally stepped on the toes of the major financial players, so they finally decided I was worth their serious attention.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: It was fine as long as they weren't paying attention, but the moment they took notice, Nirvana just swatted me down like some bothersome fly...
When she finishes, Parfait sighs heavily, deflating like a punctured balloon.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: *Sigh*... it's too late for anything now. The others don't really matter much. At worst, they just lost back the money they'd made from me over the years. And when they realized the party was over, they grabbed their pitchforks and joined the mob. Can't even blame them—I'd probably do the same.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: But those friends who have actually believed in me... That's what kills me. While I was gone, they kept throwing money into Tulip Holdings, trying to help me keep it alive. I'm afraid I'll never be able to repay them, not in my entire lifetime...

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: In our line of work, everything comes down to trust and credibility. My "investment guru" halo is already tarnished beyond repair. No one will ever believe anything I do again...
The more Parfait speaks, the deeper she sinks into her chair, as if trying to disappear entirely.
Then wouldn't all the effort you made traveling all this way back here be completely wasted?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Hey, that's not right. How is it wasted?
Parfait suddenly straightens up, pointing to the envelop filled with tickets on the table.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I never expected to salvage anything anyway. Otherwise, how could I have stayed in the Outlands for half a year...

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: This time, I'm just back to take my friends to the Spring Concert. As long as I achieve that goal, that's all that matters. Everything else is already beyond my control, no matter how hard I try.

Parfait's answer leaves you stunned. Could there really be financial criminals in this world who return to cities where they're wanted—not to clear their name or save their business, but just to attend a concert?
Then again, you recall your first meeting with Parfait on the sand ship, where she seemed to have said the same thing.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Speaking of which, I actually came back specifically for this year's Spring Concert. A fine gentleman as yourself surely wouldn't miss it, would you?
steps.female_content: Speaking of which, I actually came back specifically for this year's Spring Concert. A fine lady as yourself surely wouldn't miss it, would you?

steps.content: Well, no matter how absurd her reason might be, she's been completely honest with you about everything. At least right now, she has no reason to lie.
But... Rayden and the others said they didn't want to go to the concert...

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: WHAT?!
Parfait springs from her seat, her voice shooting up an octave.
Their exact words were: they're not interested in the concert, and given their... well, their status, they'd probably just get looks from the wealthy crowd if they went.
Despite claiming to quote them exactly, you still try to make their expression sound less harsh than it actually was.
Rayden mentioned you're always welcome back. Whatever crisis you're dealing with right now, as long as they're around, you'll never be...

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: No, no...
Before you can finish, Parfait cuts you off with visible agitation.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Wait, hold on! But this is never about status!

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: This is the Spring Concert, DisCity's crown jewel of New Year celebrations! Not to mention this year features the most dazzling lineup in history, topped with Maestro Euragio's farewell performance!

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: If I could attend just one live event in my entire life, this would be it. At this level of artistry? It's not just a performance, it's a legacy. What does wealth or social status matter when history's being made?!
Seeing your silence, Parfait suddenly slumps back into her chair.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I don't care how, but you've got to help me out.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Let my reputation be ruined. I've had my fill of glory anyway. After the concert, I'll cooperate with any investigation... Hand me over to Nirvana in chains if you must, I won't resist.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: But this concert is the one thing I cannot miss. And I especially can't bear the thought of my friends missing it... Please, could you do me this favor and try to convince them for me?
Seeing the former investment guru throw all composure to the wind, practically demanding your help with such undignified desperation, you can't decide whether to laugh or pity her.
In a way, she and her friends are remarkably alike. At least when it comes to asking for your help, neither shows any reservations.
...Okay, I'll see what I can do.
